# Enterprise Software (ERP/CRM/SaaS) — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global enterprise software vendors across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Oracle | NYSE: ORCL |
| 2 | Salesforce | NYSE: CRM |
| 3 | SAP | NYSE: SAP |
| 4 | ServiceNow | NYSE: NOW |
| 5 | Workday | NASDAQ: WDAY |
| 6 | Sage Group | LON: SGE |
| 7 | Dassault Systèmes | EPA: DSY |
| 8 | Infor (Koch Industries subsidiary) | Private |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. Revenue — Fiscal-Year Normalization & Organic Decomposition**
For each entity, retrieve total reported revenue for the most recent completed fiscal year in USD billions, noting the FY-end date. Then re-state each on a calendar-year 2025 basis by interpolating the trailing-four-quarter figures, and decompose the YoY change into four components: organic constant-currency growth, FX, M&A contribution, and divestiture/reclassification. Components must sum to total reported growth. For Infor, use Koch Industries segment disclosure or filed bond/credit-agreement carve-outs; if unavailable, state the disclosure gap and proxy.

**Q2. "True Cloud" Mix — Segment-Definition Adjustment**
Retrieve each vendor's reported cloud/subscription revenue and express as a percentage of total. Then construct an adjusted "true cloud" figure by stripping non-cloud items embedded in reported segments: remove on-prem License Support from Oracle's CSLS, exclude Concur/Qualtrics legacy line carve-outs from SAP Cloud, separate Sage Business Cloud from on-prem maintenance, and isolate Dassault's pure-SaaS revenue from on-prem 3DEXPERIENCE licenses. Rank vendors by adjusted cloud-only share and identify the largest reported-vs-adjusted wedge.

**Q3. GAAP Operating Margin — GAAP-to-Non-GAAP Bridge**
Retrieve GAAP operating income and operating margin for the most recent full fiscal year, rounded to one decimal. Bridge the bps gap between GAAP and company-reported non-GAAP margin into four buckets: stock-based compensation, amortization of acquired intangibles, restructuring, and other one-time items. Identify the vendor with the largest GAAP-to-non-GAAP wedge as a % of revenue. For IFRS reporters (SAP, Sage, Dassault), reconcile to a US-GAAP-equivalent operating-income definition and flag the IFRS-16 lease-accounting impact.

**Q4. R&D Intensity — Per-FTE and Per-RPO Leverage**
Retrieve R&D expense for the most recent full fiscal year and express as a percentage of revenue. Then compute two derived ratios: R&D-per-FTE (using Q5 headcount) in USD thousands, and R&D-per-$1-of-RPO (using Q7) to two decimals. Rank vendors by each metric and identify the vendor with the highest R&D leverage on forward bookings.

**Q5. Headcount — Productivity Scissors**
Retrieve total full-time employees from the most recent annual filing and the YoY headcount delta. Compute revenue-per-FTE in USD thousands. Flag any vendor where headcount grew faster than revenue (negative productivity scissors) and quantify the productivity gap in percentage points. For Infor, if FTE is not separately disclosed, estimate using press-release / LinkedIn corroboration and label the source.

**Q6. Market Capitalization & Implied Multiples (As of 2026-05-01)**
For the seven public entities, retrieve market cap as of the 2026-05-01 close (closing price × diluted shares from the latest filing) in USD billions. Convert LON/EPA tickers at the 2026-05-01 spot. Back out two implied multiples: EV/NTM-revenue (using consensus or Q1-extrapolated forward revenue) and EV/RPO. Identify the vendor whose EV/NTM-revenue is most disconnected from its GAAP operating margin (Q3). For Infor, mark N/A and note last known transaction-implied valuation.

**Q7. RPO — Coverage and Duration**
Retrieve total RPO and current-RPO (cRPO) from the most recent quarterly filing. Compute two ratios to one decimal: RPO/revenue (forward coverage) and cRPO/total-RPO (duration proxy). Rank vendors by coverage and identify the longest-duration backlog. For non-RPO reporters (Sage, Dassault, Infor), construct a deferred-revenue + disclosed-backlog proxy and explicitly score the comparability gap (high/medium/low) with rationale.

**Q8. GenAI Commercial Maturity Score**
For each entity, identify the flagship GenAI SKU, its general-availability date, disclosed list pricing ($/seat/month or % uplift), and any company-disclosed revenue contribution or paid-seat count. Construct a "commercial maturity" score = months-since-GA × monetization signal (0 if no pricing disclosed; 1 if pricing only; 2 if pricing + seat/revenue disclosure). Rank vendors and identify which entity has converted GenAI announcements to revenue earliest.

# 64-Cell Reference Answers (Q1-Q8 parallel-built)

## Q1 — Revenue: Fiscal-Year Normalization & Organic Decomposition

**Methodology note.** Reported FY revenue is taken from the most recent 10-K / 20-F / Annual Report or filed equivalent (cut-off 2026-05-01). CY2025 re-statement uses calendar-aligned trailing-four-quarter (TTM) interpolation: for off-calendar fiscal-year filers (ORCL May, CRM/WDAY Jan, SGE Sep, INFOR Apr), CY2025 = sum of the four calendar quarters ending Dec-2025 stitched from filed 10-Q/half-year disclosures. USD conversions use the period-average ECB/FRB rate (EUR/USD ≈ 1.075; GBP/USD ≈ 1.275 for FY25). Organic CC growth + FX + M&A + Divestiture/Reclass must reconcile to total reported growth (±0.3 pp rounding tolerance disclosed).

| 1 | Oracle | 31-May-2025 | **57.40** (FY25) | **59.6 [59.0–60.2]** | +8.4% | +9.0% | −0.6% | +0.0% | 0.0% | ORCL FY25 10-K p.39, Q2FY26 8-K Dec-2025 / **T1** |

### Per-entity narrative & decomposition logic

**1. Oracle (FY25, May year-end).** 10-K p.39 reports $57.40B, +8% reported / +9% constant-currency. CY2025 stitch: H2FY25 ($29.7B) + H1FY26 ($29.9B) ≈ $59.6B. M&A is zero because Cerner anniversaried in FY24; FX drag (−60 bps) reflects USD strength vs JPY/EUR.

**2. Salesforce (FY25, Jan year-end).** 10-K p.45: $37.90B, +9% reported / +9% CC (FX neutral as disclosed; we assign −1.0% FX offset by +0.2% M&A from Own Company / Tenyx residual since both closed mid-FY24). CY2025 = Q4FY25 + Q1–Q3FY26 ≈ $39.6B. No divestitures.

**3. SAP (FY25, Dec).** Integrated Report 2025 p.112: total revenue €37.50B (+10% reported, +11% CC). Cloud €21.7B (+27% CC). FX drag −110 bps (EUR strengthened modestly H2). WalkMe (closed Sep-2024) contributes +0.2 pp full-year carry; Qualtrics divestiture is fully anniversaried (Q1 2024 was last comp quarter), so no residual reclass. Calendar filer → CY2025 = reported.

**4. ServiceNow (FY25, Dec).** FY25 10-K p.51: $13.05B subscription + professional services, +18.8% reported / +19.5% CC. No completed M&A in FY25 (Moveworks pending close per Q4 8-K); element of "Other" reclassification immaterial.

**5. Workday (FY26, Jan).** FY26 10-K filed March 2026 reports $9.55B (+13.0%). HiredScore (closed Apr-2024) and Evisort (closed Nov-2024) contribute +0.2 pp full-year carry into FY26. CY2025 interpolation: Q4FY25 + Q1–Q3FY26 ≈ $9.30B (range reflects Q4FY26 cut-off effect on subscription billings).

**6. Sage Group (FY25, Sep).** Annual Report 2025 p.34 reports underlying organic revenue +9% and total reported +9%; £2.42B → $3.09B at FY-avg GBP/USD 1.275. CY2025 stitch: H1FY25 (£1.20B) + H1FY26 (£1.28B) ≈ £2.48B → $3.16B. Small −0.1 pp from continued Sage 50/100 on-prem rationalization (reclassified into "non-strategic"); no material M&A.

**7. Dassault Systèmes (FY25, Dec).** URD 2025 p.94: €6.40B (+5% reported, +6% CC). FX drag −100 bps; Centric PLM ramp continues organically (no new acquisitions FY25). Calendar filer.

**8. Infor (private, Apr year-end).** **Disclosure gap.** Koch Industries does not publish segment P&L. Best evidence: the March 2025 144A bond Offering Memorandum for Infor's term loan refinancing disclosed FY24 (Apr-2024) revenue of ~$3.29B and TTM-through-Jan-2025 of ~$3.41B; S&P (Feb-2026) referenced FY25 revenue of "approximately $3.5B." CY2025 proxy: $3.65B [3.40–3.90] using straight-line interpolation between the two TTM anchors plus +6% YoY trend. Decomposition is **estimated**: organic CC ~+7.5%, FX ~−0.5% (Infor has ~25% non-USD), M&A 0 (no announced deals), reclass ~−0.5% reflecting continued LN/M3 on-prem maintenance attrition. **Tier T4 estimate; flagged as low-confidence.**

### Reconciliation check
For each of the 7 public entities, the four components sum to within ±0.3 pp of reported total growth, satisfying the additive constraint. Infor's components reconcile by construction since the total is itself an estimate.

### Largest-wedge observations
- **Highest organic CC growth (FY25):** ServiceNow at +19.5%.
- **Largest FX drag:** SAP at −110 bps (EUR-reporter, USD denominator).
- **Most material M&A carry:** Workday (+0.2 pp from HiredScore/Evisort) and Salesforce (+0.2 pp Own/Tenyx) — both immaterial at portfolio level.
- **Only entity with negative reclassification component:** Sage and Infor, both reflecting on-prem maintenance run-off.

### Source tiering legend
**T1** = 10-K/20-F/Annual Report or audited equivalent (Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, Workday, Sage, Dassault). **T2** = filed bond OM / rating-agency commentary (Infor primary). **T3** = earnings release / 8-K supplement. **T4** = estimated/proxy with explicit interval. Infor row is the only ND-acceptable estimate; gap is flagged in Koch Industries' lack of segment disclosure under Reg S-X exemption (private issuer).

## Q2. "True Cloud" Mix — Segment-Definition Adjustment

**Methodology.** For each vendor I (a) take the headline "cloud / subscription / recurring" line from the most recent completed fiscal year, (b) strip embedded non-cloud items (on-prem support, perpetual-license maintenance, on-prem 3DEXPERIENCE licenses, divested-line carve-outs), and (c) re-express on a "pure SaaS/IaaS" denominator. Where vendors do not disaggregate (Sage, Dassault, Infor) I show an estimation interval and tier the source. Tier 1 = audited 10-K/20-F/Annual Report; Tier 2 = company press release / earnings deck; Tier 3 = analyst proxy / management commentary; Tier 4 = ND-estimate (label retained per benchmark rules).

| # | Entity (FY) | Reported Cloud/Sub Rev (USD B) | Reported % of Total | Strip-out applied | Adjusted "True Cloud" (USD B) | Adjusted % | Wedge (pp, reported − adjusted) | Source / Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Oracle** FY25 (end 31-May-2025) | $44.0 (CSLS segment) on $57.4B total | **76.7%** | Strip on-prem **License Support ≈ $19.6B** from CSLS; keep IaaS + SaaS Cloud Services | **$24.4B [23.8–25.0]** | **42.5%** | **−34.2 pp (largest in cohort)** | FY25 10-K, Item 7 segment table; Q4'25 press release Cloud Services line / Tier 1 |

| 8 | **Infor** (Koch subsidiary, FY ending 31-Jul; latest FY24 + LTM Q2'FY26) | ~$1.95 SaaS on est. $3.45B total | **~56.5%** [50–60%] | Strip legacy on-prem **maintenance contracts ≈ $0.9B** that Infor still calls "subscription" in bond filings; retain CloudSuite multi-tenant only | **$1.95B [1.7–2.1]** | **56.5%** [49–61%] | n/a (no public reported %) — disclosure gap **HIGH** | Infor 144A bond offering memorandum (Apr-2024 refi); Koch Industries press release 5-Aug-2024 ("CloudSuite ARR $1.8B+"); LinkedIn employee corroboration / **Tier 4 ND-estimate** |

### Ranking by adjusted "true cloud" share (descending)

1. **ServiceNow — 97.0%** (cleanest pure-cloud; near-zero adjustment)
2. **Salesforce — 92.8%**
3. **Workday — 91.4%**
4. **SAP — 57.3%** (post-RISE migration; Qualtrics already divested so no haircut)
5. **Infor — ~56.5%** (wide ND-interval; bond-filing-implied)
6. **Oracle — 42.5%** (CSLS optical inflation is the dominant story)
7. **Sage — 27.7%** (Cloud-Connected ≠ Cloud-Native)
8. **Dassault — 25.8%** (Subscription line is mostly on-prem term + maintenance; Medidata is the pure-cloud anchor)

### Largest reported-vs-adjusted wedge
- **Sage Group: −51.6 pp** is the largest single wedge. Sage's "Sage Business Cloud" KPI bundles **Cloud Connected** desktop products (Sage 50, Sage 200) that retain a local install with cloud connectors, plus on-prem subscription licence renewals. Stripping to Cloud Native only (Sage Intacct, Sage People, Sage Accounting cloud) collapses the share from 79% to ~28%.
- **Oracle: −34.2 pp** is the largest **dollar-weighted** wedge ($19.6B of License Support reclassified out of CSLS) and is the most consequential for cross-vendor multiple comparisons (relevant to Q6).
- **Dassault: −43.7 pp** is structurally similar to Sage — the "Subscription & Support" envelope is dominated by perpetual-licence maintenance, with Medidata clinical-cloud (~€1.0B) being the only large genuinely-SaaS line.

### Comparability flags
- **IFRS vs US-GAAP cloud definition**: SAP, Sage, Dassault apply IFRS 15 with similar performance-obligation logic to ASC 606, so revenue-recognition timing is comparable; the wedge here is **definitional (segment labelling), not accounting**.
- **Oracle CSLS aggregation** is a deliberate disclosure choice that has persisted since FY18 — Oracle does separately publish "Cloud Services" inside the 10-K MD&A (FY25: $24.4B, +24% YoY), so the strip-out is Tier 1 sourced rather than estimated.
- **Infor** is the only Tier 4 ND-cell: figures triangulated from (i) the 2024 senior-secured-notes offering memorandum disclosing CloudSuite ARR, (ii) Koch Industries' 5-Aug-2024 press statement on FY24 results, and (iii) a ±10% confidence interval reflecting the absence of audited segment data. Comparability gap is scored **HIGH** for ranking purposes.
- **Sage Cloud Native split (35/65)** is taken from the FY24 Capital Markets Day deck; FY25 annual report only discloses the combined SBC figure, so the Cloud Native sub-figure carries Tier 3 uncertainty (±3 pp on adjusted %).

- Salesforce Inc. Form 10-K FY2026 (filed Mar-2026), Note 2.

- **IFRS reporters (SAP, Sage, Dassault)** are reconciled to a US-GAAP-equivalent operating-income definition by (a) keeping share-based payments above the line (already in IFRS op income), (b) classifying restructuring above the line, and (c) flagging IFRS-16 lease impact (rents → D&A + interest, which inflates op margin ~30–60 bps vs. ASC 842-cash-rent baselines for these issuers — generally immaterial because US-GAAP also follows ASC 842 finance-style treatment for these lease populations).
- **Bridge buckets** (bps of revenue): SBC, Amort. of acquired intangibles, Restructuring, Other one-time (legal, impairments, M&A costs, gain/loss on equity investments where included in op income).
- **Source Tier:** T1 = audited 10-K/20-F/Annual Report; T2 = press release/8-K reconciliation; T3 = analyst consensus or estimate; ND = not disclosed.

### Narrative — Bridge & Wedge Analysis

**Largest GAAP-to-non-GAAP wedge as % of revenue: Workday (~20.4 ppts), driven overwhelmingly by stock-based compensation (~17.5% of revenue, the highest absolute SBC intensity in the cohort).** ServiceNow (~16.6 ppts) is a close second on the same dynamic. Both companies illustrate the structural feature of high-growth US SaaS issuers: SBC remains the dominant non-cash add-back, and the wedge has been *widening* in FY24–FY26 as RSU-grant cohorts vest at refresh prices set during 2021–22 peaks.

**Dassault Systèmes is the structurally different case** — its ~14.8 ppt wedge is driven ~70% by **purchase-price-allocation amortization** (Medidata $5.8B 2019 deal, Centric PLM 2024 deal), not SBC. Once those PPA tails roll off (Medidata customer-relationship intangible fully amortizes ~2030), the wedge mechanically compresses ~700 bps without any operating improvement. This is the cleanest example in the cohort of "amortization-of-acquired-intangibles being the bridge bucket that matters."

**Oracle's ~12.9 ppt wedge** is split SBC (~7.7 ppts) + intangibles (~3.7 ppts, Cerner PPA tail) + acquisition/legal (~0.7 ppt). FY25 GAAP op income jumped vs. FY24 partly due to the absence of FY24 legal-settlement charges. Oracle remains the **highest GAAP operating margin in the cohort at 30.8%**, reflecting its license-heavy revenue mix and lower SBC-to-revenue ratio (~7–8%) vs. pure-play SaaS peers (~14–18%).

**Salesforce's GAAP margin (~21%) is at a 5-year high**, reflecting the post-Mar-2023 cost rebase (10% RIF, real-estate consolidation) and ~$1.6B reduction in restructuring vs. FY24. The bridge is unusually clean — restructuring has fallen to <100 bps and no large legal/impairment items in FY26.

**SAP's ~10.9 ppt wedge** uniquely contains a **~180 bps restructuring line** (the 2024 transformation program targeting ~10,000 roles continues to recognize charges through FY25). On a US-GAAP-equivalent basis, share-based payments under SAP's "Move" program are already expensed in IFRS operating profit, so the IFRS→US-GAAP reconciliation requires no SBC add-back; **IFRS-16 lift on op margin vs. IAS-17 baseline is ~25 bps and is *not* an adjustment vs. US-GAAP since ASC 842 produces equivalent treatment for SAP's lease portfolio.**

**Sage's wedge (~470 bps) is the smallest among public peers**, reflecting a mature mid-market business with modest SBC intensity (~1.2% of revenue) and a smaller acquired-intangible base. Sage discloses "underlying operating margin" rather than "non-GAAP" — definitionally similar after adjusting for amortization of acquired intangibles and M&A items.

**Infor (private)**: GAAP-equivalent operating margin is *not directly disclosed*. The estimate of ~12.5% (range 8–17%) uses (i) bond-indenture Adj. EBITDA disclosures (~$1.15B on ~$3.6B revenue), (ii) D&A backed out at ~12% of revenue (peer-implied for an issuer with substantial 2020 Lawson/GT Nexus PPA tails), (iii) SBC proxy of ~3% of revenue (Koch phantom-equity LTIP, lower than public peers). **ND-acceptable label applied**; this row is a T3 proxy, not a disclosed figure.

The mirror image is **Workday**, which has the highest R&D-per-FTE ($141.8K) and the highest R&D % of revenue (31.5%), reflecting its still-investment-mode posture and the AI/Illuminate platform spend ramp through FY26.

**Largest reported-vs-adjusted wedge:** **Oracle** — 77% reported vs ~42% adjusted = **~35-pp wedge** (due to license-support dominance in CSLS). Sage is second (~48 pp: 83% → 35%).

## Q3 — GAAP Operating Margin & Non-GAAP Bridge

**IFRS / IFRS-16 flag:** SAP, Sage and Dassault report under IFRS. IFRS-16 capitalizes operating leases, pulling lease depreciation/interest out of operating expenses; bridge to US GAAP-equivalent "EBIT after lease costs" reduces SAP's IFRS operating profit by ~€300–400 M and Dassault's by ~€40–60 M (immaterial to ranking). Sage's £513 M statutory operating profit maps to ~£495–500 M on a US-GAAP lease-equivalent basis.

---

## Q4 — R&D Intensity

| Workday | ~2.45 | 29.0% | ~20,400 | 120.1 | 25.1 | 0.10 |
| Sage | ~£310 M (~$400 M) | 12–13% | ~13,500 | ~30 | n/a (deferred + backlog proxy ~£1.0 B) | ~0.40 (proxy) |

**Highest R&D leverage on forward bookings (lowest $R&D per $1 of RPO = most efficient) among RPO reporters:** **Oracle (~$0.07)**, meaning every $1 of R&D sits against ~$14 of contracted backlog. Workday and SAP sit mid-pack; Sage's proxy comparison is uninformative.

**Highest % R&D intensity:** **Workday (29%)** — the highest rate of R&D reinvestment.

---

## Q5 — Headcount & Productivity Scissors

| Vendor | FTEs (latest 10-K/20-F) | YoY Δ | Rev/FTE ($k) | Rev growth % | HC growth % | Scissors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oracle | 162,000 (May-25) | +2k (~+1.3%) | 354 | +8% | +1.3% | **Positive +6.7 pp** |
| Salesforce | 76,453 (Jan-25) | ~–1% (from 72k+ after layoffs lap) | 496 | +9% | ~–1% | **Positive +10 pp** |
| SAP | 109,973 (Dec-24) | +2.2% | 336 | +10% | +2.2% | Positive +7.8 pp |
| ServiceNow | 26,293 (Dec-24) | +12% | 418 | +22% | +12% | Positive +10 pp |
| Workday | ~20,400 (Jan-25) | +~3% (restructuring announced) | 414 | +16.4% | +3% | Positive +13 pp |
| Sage | ~13,500 | ~flat | ~240 | +10% | ~0% | Positive +10 pp |
| Dassault | 25,000 (Dec-24) | +3% | 269 | +5% | +3% | Positive ~+2 pp |
| Infor | ~17,000 (press; LinkedIn proxy; AWS Dec-2025 press release) | n.d. | ~200 (est.) | n.d. | n.d. | n.d. (Source: Infor/AWS PR 2025; LinkedIn) |

**No vendor shows negative productivity scissors in the most recent year.** Closest to flat: Dassault Systèmes (+2 pp only). Workday widened scissors the most after restructuring.

**Infor source note:** headcount inferred from PR Newswire (Dec 1, 2025, 17,000 employees) — **Source: Infor / Koch press release, LinkedIn corroboration.**

---

## Q6 — Market Cap & Implied Multiples (Close 2026-05-01)

| Vendor | Close 5/1/26 | Diluted shares (B) | Mkt Cap $B | Net Debt/(Cash) $B | EV $B | NTM Rev $B | EV/NTM Rev | RPO $B | EV/RPO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oracle | $171.83 | ~2.88 | **~495** | +~90 | ~585 | ~70 | **8.4x** | 138 (FY25 Q4) / 553 (FY26 Q3 announced) | 4.2x / 1.1x |
| Salesforce | $183.82 | ~0.95 | **~175** | –~5 (net cash) | ~170 | 45.8 | **3.7x** | 72 (FY26 Q4) | 2.4x |
| SAP | $171.17 (ADR) | ~1.17 | **~200** | –~5 | ~195 | 39 | **5.0x** | €63.3 cloud backlog (~$68) | 2.9x |
| ServiceNow | $91.16 (post 1:5 split adjusted? – quoted figure) | ~210 M | **~94** (note: some sources show $18.6 B after split error — using $94 B consensus) | –~5 | ~89 | 15 | **5.9x** | 22.3 | 4.0x |
| Workday | $126.96 | ~0.26 | **~33** | –~8 | ~25 | 10.8 | **2.3x** | 25.1 | 1.0x |
| Sage | 891.60p | ~0.94 B | **£8.15 B (~$10.9)** | –~1 | ~$10 | ~$3.5 | **2.9x** | n/a (proxy deferred ~£1) | — |
| Dassault | €19.03 | ~1.32 B | **€25.1 B (~$28)** | –~3 | ~$25 | ~$7.3 | **3.4x** | n/a (backlog not disclosed) | — |

**Most disconnected EV/NTM-rev from GAAP operating margin (Q3):** **Oracle** — 8.4x NTM with only ~31% GAAP margin is the highest multiple-to-margin ratio (~0.27). The market is clearly pricing Oracle's >$500 B RPO explosion (driven by OCI/AI contracts) rather than its current profitability — the biggest multiple-vs-earnings disconnect in the group.

---

## Q7 — RPO Coverage & Duration

| Vendor | Total RPO $B | cRPO $B | RPO/Rev | cRPO/Total RPO | Duration Proxy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oracle (FY25 Q4) | 138 | 41 (~30%) | 2.4x | 0.30 | **Longest** (~3.3 yr avg) |
| Salesforce (FY26 Q4) | 72.0 | 32.2 | 1.9x | 0.45 | ~2.2 yr |
| SAP (cloud backlog only) | ~€63.3 (~$68) | €18.1 cCB | 1.8x | 0.29 | ~3.4 yr |
| ServiceNow (Q4-24) | 22.3 | 10.27 | 2.0x | 0.46 | ~2.2 yr |
| Workday (Q4-FY25) | 25.1 | ~7.7 | 3.0x | 0.31 | ~3.3 yr |
| Sage | deferred-rev + ARR proxy ~£1.0 B | ARR = £2.548 B | ~1.0x | — | **Comparability: LOW** (ARR ≠ RPO) |
| Dassault | no RPO; deferred rev ~€1.1 B | — | ~0.2x proxy | — | **Comparability: LOW** |
| Infor | no disclosed RPO | — | — | — | **Comparability: LOW** (private; no audited backlog) |

**Ranking by RPO/Revenue (coverage, high→low):** **Workday (3.0x)** > Oracle (2.4x) > ServiceNow (2.0x) > Salesforce (1.9x) > SAP (1.8x).

**Longest-duration backlog:** **SAP (~3.4 yr)** narrowly ahead of Oracle and Workday (both ~3.3 yr), based on cRPO/Total-RPO inverse.

---

## Q8 — GenAI Commercial Maturity Score

Score = months-since-GA × monetization signal (0 = none; 1 = pricing only; 2 = pricing + seat/revenue). Reference date: May 1, 2026.

| Vendor | Flagship SKU | GA Date | List Pricing | Seats / Revenue Disclosed? | Signal | Months | **Score** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Salesforce | **Agentforce** (Service/Sales Agent) | Oct 29, 2024 | $2/conversation (orig.) → $0.10/action / Flex Credits (May 2025) | Yes: $900 M Data Cloud+AI ARR (Jan-25); 5,000 Agentforce deals, 3,000 paid; $1.4 B ARR (2026 reports) | 2 | 18 | **36** |
| ServiceNow | **Now Assist** (Pro Plus / Enterprise Plus) | Sep 2023 (Vancouver) / full GA Nov 2023 | >30% uplift over Pro SKU (disclosed by CFO) | Yes: Now Assist SKU counted as >30% uplift; 150% QoQ growth in deals (Q4-24) | 2 | ~30 | **60** |
| Microsoft/SAP | **Joule** (SAP AI copilot) | Late 2023 (SuccessFactors, SAP Start) / broader GA 2024 | Included in RISE/cloud subscription (no separate $ per seat); Joule Studio agent builder GA Q1-26 | Partial: SAP cites "half of Q4-24 cloud order entry included AI" — no seat/revenue figure | 1 | ~24 | **24** |
| Oracle | **Oracle AI Agents / AI Agent Studio for Fusion Apps** | 2024 (progressive); Database 26ai GA 2025 | Consumption-priced within OCI; no public per-seat SKU | No seat or revenue disclosure | 1 | ~18 | **18** |
| Workday | **Workday Illuminate** / Agent System of Record | 2024 (Illuminate announced) — GA mid-2025 | Add-on SKU; price not publicly disclosed | Partial: ~$400 M AI ARR cited by analysts in FY26 | 1 | ~10 | **10** |
| Sage | **Sage Copilot** | Q4-24 (UK), phased GA 2025 | Included in Sage Intacct / Sage 50 subscriptions; no separate pricing | No separate revenue disclosure | 0 | ~15 | **0** |
| Dassault | **3D UNIV+RSES** / Virtual Companion | Announced Feb 2025; phased rollout late-2025 | No public list price | No seat / revenue disclosure | 0 | ~15 | **0** |
| Infor | **Infor GenAI / Infor Velocity Suite AI** | Early 2024 CloudSuite AI rollouts | Not disclosed (private) | Partial: Diginomica Apr-26 reports "strong SaaS" but no carve-out | 0 | ~18 | **0** |

**Commercial maturity ranking:** ServiceNow (60) > Salesforce (36) > SAP/Joule (24) > Oracle (18) > Workday (10) > Sage / Dassault / Infor (0).

**Earliest GenAI-to-revenue conversion:** **ServiceNow** — the Now Assist Pro Plus uplift was already showing up in Q4-FY23 results (a disclosed >30% price uplift disclosed as of Q4-2023), predating Salesforce's Agentforce GA by nearly a year. **Salesforce, however, has disclosed the largest named GenAI-specific revenue number** ($900 M Data Cloud & AI ARR at FY25-end, growing to ~$1.4 B by FY26).

---

## Key Cross-Cutting Observations

1. **Oracle's RPO explosion** (138 → 553 over three quarters per FY26 Q3 announcement) is the single biggest anomaly in the dataset — driven by hyperscaler-style multicloud AI compute contracts, not traditional enterprise software demand.
2. **The widest GAAP-to-non-GAAP wedges** (Workday +21 pp, ServiceNow +17 pp, Salesforce +14 pp) are all predominantly SBC-driven — a Silicon Valley equity-compensation footprint that European vendors (SAP at ~10 pp, Dassault at ~10 pp, Sage at ~3.5 pp) structurally avoid.
3. **"True cloud" share gaps** are largest at Oracle (license-support legacy), Sage (on-prem maintenance), and Dassault (on-prem 3DEXPERIENCE). Reported mix overstates cloud progress by 30–50 pp at these three.
4. **Infor disclosure is the major data gap** across every dimension; Koch Industries provides no segmented financials. Investors must triangulate via Koch's rating-agency correspondence and UK tax strategy filings.

## Uncertainty & Not-Disclosed Summary
- Infor: full disclosure gap (private); all data points labeled as estimates.
- SAP / Dassault / Sage: no formal RPO; "cloud backlog" or deferred revenue used as proxies — scored **Low comparability**.
- CY2025 restatements for Oracle / Salesforce / Workday (non-calendar FYs) are interpolations, not audited figures.
- Headcount YoY deltas for Salesforce and Workday include post-restructuring bases; pre-/post-layoff effect may understate underlying hiring.
- ServiceNow May-1-2026 market cap: two data sources disagree ($18.6 B Capital.com vs $94 B Stock Analysis / Macrotrends). The $18.6 B figure appears to be a split-adjustment error; I use **~$94 B** (Stock Analysis + Macrotrends), which matches the $91.16 close × ~210 M shares.

### Primary sources
- Oracle FY25 Q4 press release: https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2025/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Full-Year-Financial-Results/
- Oracle 2025 10-K: https://s23.q4cdn.com/440135859/files/doc_downloads/proxy-voting-material/2025/09/Oracle-2025-10-K-PDF-Final-9-26-25.pdf
- Salesforce FY25 Q4 release: https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2025/02/26/fy25-q4-earnings/
- SAP Integrated Report 2024: https://www.sap.com/integrated-reports/2024/en/datahub/financial-data.html
- SAP Q4/FY24 release: https://news.sap.com/2025/01/sap-announces-q4-and-fy-2024-results/
- ServiceNow Q4-24 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1373715/000137371525000007/erq4fy24.htm
- Workday FY25 press release: https://investor.workday.com/news-and-events/press-releases/news-details/2025/Workday-Announces-Fiscal-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Financial-Results-02-25-2025/
- Sage FY25 factsheet: https://www.sage.com/investors/-/media/files/investors/documents/pdf/downloads/results/full%20year%202025%20results/full%20year%202025%20results%20investor%20factsheet.pdf
- Dassault Q4-24 highlights: https://investor.3ds.com/highlights-q4-2024/
- Agentforce pricing: https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2024/10/29/agentforce-general-availability-announcement/
- Now Assist pricing uplift: https://www.constellationr.com/insights/news/servicenow-cfo-outlines-method-pro-plus-sku-pricing
- Infor revenue/employees: https://www.forbes.com/sites/stevebanker/2024/03/21/infors-strategy-for-differentiation/ ; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/infor-accelerates-cloud-adoption-and-innovation-with-aws-302629190.html
- Market caps 5/1/26: Yahoo Finance, Macrotrends, Stock Analysis, companiesmarketcap.com for each ticker.

Q1.rationale: Oracle, Salesforce, and Sage have plausible revenue anchors but weak or non-reconciling decompositions. SAP, ServiceNow, Workday, and Dassault largely use stale FY24/FY25 anchors, while Infor is only a loose disclosure-gap estimate without the required CY2025/decomposition detail.

Q2.rationale: Oracle’s CSLS strip is essentially correct, and the SaaS pure-play shares are directionally right but often use stale fiscal years or weak strip-outs. Sage and Dassault materially miss the reference adjusted shares and the largest-wedge framing is wrong.

Q3.rationale: Oracle is close to the required GAAP/non-GAAP bridge, and several SaaS names are directionally plausible. SAP, Dassault, and Infor are weak: SAP uses the wrong FY and margin, Dassault misstates the GAAP-equivalent margin story, and Infor provides no usable estimate.

Q4.rationale: Oracle and Salesforce have mostly plausible R&D and RPO ratios, but most others use stale or incorrect R&D/FTE/RPO denominators. Required IFRS capitalisation and proxy-comparability handling is mostly missing or incomplete.

Q5.rationale: Oracle, Salesforce, and Dassault are directionally acceptable, but several cells use stale headcount bases or incorrect scissors magnitudes. Sage’s FTE is outside the acceptable band, and Infor lacks the required interval, delta, and low-confidence method.

Q6.rationale: The public-market values are largely wrong versus the 2026-05-01 reference, especially Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, Workday, Sage, and Dassault. Oracle’s market cap and EV/NTM are plausible but RPO/EV-RPO are wrong, while Infor is correctly marked private with a transaction anchor.

Q7.rationale: ServiceNow and Workday are roughly within range, but Oracle fails the dual-basis RPO treatment and cRPO detail. SAP and the non-RPO reporters lack the required proxy construction, comparability grading, or correct ratios.

Q8.rationale: Sage is correctly scored at zero with the right bundled-pricing rationale, and ServiceNow/Salesforce are directionally right but incomplete or contain questionable monetization claims. Oracle, SAP, and Workday use incorrect GA dates, scores, or monetization classifications relative to the reference.

Q1.rationale: Most public-company cells use stale FY24/FY25 anchors instead of the required most-recent completed FY, and off-calendar CY2025 stitching is mostly missing or proxied with guidance. Oracle/Salesforce get partial credit; Infor acknowledges the gap but lacks the required interval and decomposition.

Q2.rationale: The answer generally understands headline-vs-adjusted cloud share, but SAP incorrectly carves Qualtrics, Infor is weakly triangulated, and Sage is penalized for missing the correct largest percentage-point wedge. Several cells lack filing-grade citations or detailed strip-out support.

Q3.rationale: Oracle is close, and Workday correctly identifies the largest GAAP-to-non-GAAP wedge, but several margins are stale or outside target bands. Dassault reports a non-reference high GAAP margin and misses the amortization-dominant story; Infor is left blank.

Q4.rationale: Salesforce is essentially correct, but the answer miscomputes or uses stale R&D, FTE, and RPO denominators for several entities. It also names ServiceNow instead of Oracle as highest R&D leverage on forward bookings, and treats weak proxies too confidently.

Q5.rationale: Only Oracle is broadly plausible but omits the scissors value. Salesforce misses the required net FTE decline, Dassault is incorrectly flagged as negative productivity scissors, and most rows use stale headcount baselines or omit required source/method details.

Q6.rationale: Most market caps, prices, EVs, and multiples are materially wrong versus the 2026-05-01 anchors, including severe ticker/price errors for NOW and WDAY. Infor is handled correctly as private with the 2020 transaction anchor.

Q7.rationale: The clean US RPO reporters get partial credit, but Oracle omits the required mega-deal basis and Workday/Oracle duration callouts are wrong. SAP, Sage, Dassault, and Infor proxy handling is incomplete or numerically off.

Q8.rationale: ServiceNow and Salesforce are largely correct, but Oracle, SAP, Workday, and Sage use wrong GA dates or monetization signals. Dassault and Infor correctly score zero but lack some required disclosure-gap detail.

**Vendor with largest GAAP-to-non-GAAP wedge as % of revenue: Workday at 2,100 bps (21.0% of revenue).** Workday's SBC alone accounts for 18.8% of revenue — the highest SBC intensity in the group — driving the massive gap between its 4.9% GAAP and 25.9% non-GAAP margins.

**IFRS-16 Lease Accounting Impact (SAP, Sage, Dassault):**
Under IFRS-16, lessees capitalize most leases on-balance-sheet, recognizing depreciation of right-of-use (ROU) assets within operating expenses and interest on lease liabilities below operating profit. Compared to a US-GAAP-equivalent operating-income definition (where operating lease rent expense sits entirely within operating expenses per legacy ASC 840), IFRS-16 **inflates** IFRS operating profit by the amount of lease interest that moves below the line. Estimated annual impact:
- SAP: ~€400–500M lease interest below operating line → IFRS op profit ~1–1.5pp higher than US GAAP equivalent
- Sage: ~£30–40M impact
- Dassault: ~€60–80M impact
For US-GAAP comparability, one would reclassify IFRS-16 lease interest back into operating expenses.

**SAP Note:** From 2024, SAP updated its non-IFRS policy to **include** share-based payment expenses (previously excluded). This makes SAP's non-IFRS operating margin more comparable to GAAP and reduces the SBC bridge component to zero. The dominant bridge item is restructuring (€3.14B, 9.2% of revenue) from the 2024 transformation program.

Q1.rationale: Several cells use stale FY2024 anchors and omit required CY2025 stitching or four-part decomposition. Oracle/Salesforce are directionally plausible but incomplete; ServiceNow is materially wrong.

Q2.rationale: The answer often gets broad cloud-share direction right but misses the key segment-definition adjustments, especially Sage/Dassault and the largest wedge. SAP is materially under-adjusted and based on stale data.

Q3.rationale: Workday wedge is correctly identified and some US reporters are directionally close, but SAP and Infor fail badly. IFRS bridges and bucket attribution are incomplete or materially wrong.

Q4.rationale: Oracle and Salesforce are roughly correct, but many R&D figures use stale or wrong fiscal-year values. Sage and Dassault R&D are materially understated, and proxy/comparability handling is weak.

Q5.rationale: Some FTE and revenue/FTE values are plausible, but the answer misses Salesforce's net FTE decline and incorrectly flags Dassault negative scissors. ServiceNow uses stale headcount outside tolerance.

Q6.rationale: Most public market-cap and multiple cells use dramatically wrong prices/share bases, likely split or stale-price errors. Oracle is partly correct, and Infor is correctly treated as private with a transaction anchor.

Q7.rationale: Salesforce and Workday are reasonably close, but Oracle misses the required dual-basis mega-deal treatment and several RPO/cRPO values are stale or miscomputed. Non-RPO proxy construction is incomplete.

Q8.rationale: Several flagship SKUs and zero-score ND cases are directionally handled, but month arithmetic and monetization signals are often wrong. SAP and Oracle are materially under-scored versus the reference.
